summary: Landed Phase 6 of plan v02 (S4KeyedHintikkaInv keys-threaded Hintikka-tracking invariant bundle + its monotonicity/weakening lemma), lean_verify-clean and sorry-free, committed as 828aefd4. Phases 7-11 (single-step preservation, top-loop induction, soundness redirect lemma, soundness top-loop, completeness/decidability) remain, per continuation handoff.
decisions_made: S4KeyedHintikkaInv carries ONLY the five Hintikka-specific conjuncts (hintikkaInv/eBoxOnlyNeg/eBoxNegWitness/eDiamondOnlyPos/eDiamondPosWitness), NOT the universe-closure/keys-bookkeeping conjuncts already covered by the frozen S4LoopInv -- threaded as a separate ambient hypothesis at each call site rather than duplicated into one struct, matching how S4LoopInv's own preservation theorem already threads keysWorldsKnown/worldsContiguousS4 as separate hypotheses rather than struct fields.

modalApplyOneT_snd_eq/modalApplyOneS4Rules_snd_eq established the accessibility-output component of the T/4-rule-augmented dispatch is UNCONDITIONALLY identical to raw K's own modalApplyOne snd (the propagation arms only ever touch .fst) -- this simplified the hasEdge-monotonicity proof considerably versus threading a full RuleApplicationSpecCore-style freshLocal field through every dispatch layer.
dead_ends: Proving `.snd` equality through modalApplyOneT/modalApplyOneS4Rules's nested let+match definitions required TWO fixes beyond the naive approach: (1) rcases on the .fst PROJECTION does not substitute into a goal whose match scrutinizes the let-bound pair variable -- must rcases the WHOLE pair via `rcases hk : (modalApplyOne sf b acc) with <kResult, kAcc>`; (2) even after that, `exact`/`rfl` can fail through an intervening `have foo := ...; match ...` binder unless a bare `dsimp only` (not `simp only [hk]`, which triggers an unused-simp-argument lint warning since the rewrite already happened via the rcases destructuring) forces the reduction first. Documented with the exact working tactic sequence in the continuation handoff to save re-discovery time in Phase 7, which will very likely need more of these.
